headline: Amazon Web Services chief Matt Garman said he feels "really good" about Amazon's AI spending and is not worried about a bubble, because most of AWS's business is ordinary computing, storage and running trained AI models.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a leading cloud executive answers the bubble debate, though it is his own business he is defending.
importance_line: Investors and companies that rely on AWS hear a reassurance from the executive in charge of that spending, so it is a company view, not an independent finding.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Garman, chief executive of Amazon's cloud arm AWS, said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast that AWS spreads its capacity across many customers and that most of its use is core computing, storage and inference (running trained AI models), workloads that "just aren't gonna go away". He likened AI start-ups to venture investing, where not every company survives, as in the internet bubble, while Yahoo notes that investor Ray Dalio warned this week that AI speculation may be near its peak, which we carried on 7 Oct 2026.
notes: Benzinga blocked; Yahoo Finance reports the podcast itself. Source is Yahoo Finance as the outlet that reported it; the podcast is the origin.
